af: Three vertical stripes — black, red and green — with a white emblem of a mosque and wheat sheaves in the middle.
ao: Red and black bands with a yellow emblem: half a cog, a machete and a star. The machete stands for farm work, the cog for factory work.
al: A red field with a black double-headed eagle. The same eagle was on the seal of Skanderbeg, the leader who defended the country in the 1400s.
ae: Green, white and black stripes with a red vertical band at the hoist — the four pan-Arab colours found on many Arab flags.
ar: Light blue, white and light blue stripes with the Sun of May in the middle — a sun with a human face, the sign of independence.
am: Red, blue and orange stripes. The orange band is usually explained as the colour of work and wheat fields.
aq: A blue field with the white outline of the continent. It is not a state flag: Antarctica has no country, and the design was made for shared use.
tf: A blue field with the French flag in the corner, the white letters TF and the stars of the Southern Cross.
au: A blue field with the British flag in the corner, the big seven-pointed Commonwealth Star and the Southern Cross.
at: Red, white and red stripes — one of the oldest flag designs in Europe, known since the 13th century.
az: Blue, red and green stripes with a white crescent and an eight-pointed star in the middle.
bi: A white diagonal cross splits the flag into red and green parts, with three red stars in a white disc in the middle.
be: Black, yellow and red vertical stripes — the colours of the old Brabant coat of arms, a gold lion on black.
bj: A green band at the hoist with yellow and red stripes beside it — the pan-African colours.
bf: Red and green bands with a yellow star in the middle.
bd: A green field with a red disc set slightly towards the hoist, so it looks centred when the flag is flying.
bg: White, green and red stripes: white for peace, green for fields and forests, red for courage.
bs: Aquamarine and gold stripes for the sea and the sand, with a black triangle at the hoist.
ba: A blue field with a yellow triangle and a line of white stars. The triangle hints at the country's three peoples and at its shape.
by: Red and green bands with a white woven pattern at the hoist, the kind embroidered on traditional towels.
bz: A blue field with red bands top and bottom and a coat of arms showing two woodcutters and a tree.
bo: Red, yellow and green stripes with the coat of arms in the middle. Bolivia also flies the wiphala, the chequered flag of its indigenous peoples.
br: A green field, a yellow diamond and a blue globe with stars and the motto “Order and Progress”. The stars show the sky over Rio on the night the republic was declared.
bn: A yellow field with white and black diagonal stripes and a red emblem in the middle.
bt: The flag is split diagonally into yellow and orange, with a white dragon clutching jewels across the middle.
bw: A light blue field with a black band edged in white. The blue stands for water, the most precious thing in a dry country.
cf: Four horizontal stripes crossed by a red vertical one, with a yellow star in the corner. The red band ties together the African and French colours.
ca: Red bands at the sides and a red maple leaf in the middle. The leaf has eleven points — just a design, not a count of provinces.
ch: A white cross on red. The Swiss flag is square — only one other country's flag is.
cl: White and red bands with a blue square and a white star at the hoist.
cn: A red field with one large yellow star and four smaller ones beside it.
ci: Orange, white and green vertical stripes — like the Irish flag, but with the colours in reverse order.
cm: Green, red and yellow vertical stripes with a yellow star in the middle.
cd: A sky-blue field with a yellow star in the corner and a red diagonal band edged in yellow.
cg: Green and red parts divided by a yellow diagonal band.
co: A yellow band filling the whole upper half, with blue and red below. Yellow is the country's gold, blue its two oceans, red the blood that was shed.
cr: Five bands: blue, white, red, white and blue again. The red one in the middle is wider than the rest.
cu: Blue and white stripes with a red triangle at the hoist holding a white star. The three blue stripes are the parts the island was once divided into.
cy: A white field with a copper-yellow outline of the island itself and two olive branches for peace.
cz: White and red bands with a blue triangle at the hoist. The blue was added so the flag would not be confused with Poland's.
de: Black, red and gold from top to bottom. These were the colours worn by volunteers who fought against Napoleon.
dj: Light blue and green bands with a white triangle at the hoist holding a red star.
dk: A white cross on red, shifted towards the hoist. The Dannebrog is considered the oldest national flag still in use.
do: A white cross divides the flag into blue and red quarters, with a coat of arms in the middle showing a cross and an open book.
dz: Green and white halves with a red crescent and star in the middle.
ec: A yellow band half the height of the flag, blue and red below, and a coat of arms with a condor and Mount Chimborazo.
eg: Red, white and black stripes with the golden Eagle of Saladin in the middle.
er: A red triangle running the length of the flag, green above and blue below, with a golden olive branch and wreath at the hoist.
es: Red, yellow and red bands, the middle one twice as wide. The yellow band carries a coat of arms with a crown and two columns.
ee: Blue, black and white stripes, chosen by students in the 19th century: blue for sky and lakes, black for the soil, white for snow.
et: Green, yellow and red bands with a blue disc and a golden star. Many African countries later took up these three colours.
fi: A blue cross on white: blue for the lakes, white for the snow.
fj: A light blue field with the British flag in the corner and a shield showing sugar cane, a palm, bananas and a dove.
fk: A blue field with the British flag in the corner and a coat of arms showing a ram and a sailing ship.
fr: Three vertical stripes: blue, white and red. Blue and red are the colours of Paris, white was the king's colour.
ga: Green, yellow and blue bands: the forest, the equator and the sea.
gb: Three crosses combined in one flag: St George's for England, St Andrew's for Scotland and St Patrick's for Ireland.
ge: A white field with a large red cross and four small crosses in the corners, going back to medieval banners.
gh: Red, gold and green bands with a black star in the middle. The black star became a symbol of African freedom.
gn: Red, yellow and green vertical stripes — the pan-African colours.
gm: Red, blue and green bands separated by white lines. The blue is the Gambia River, along which the country stretches.
gw: A red band at the hoist with a black star, and yellow and green bands beside it.
gq: Green, white and red bands, a blue triangle at the hoist and a coat of arms with a silk-cotton tree.
gr: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross in the corner. The nine stripes are linked to the syllables of an old freedom motto.
gl: White and red halves with a disc coloured the other way round: red on top, white below — the sun above the ice.
gt: Blue, white and blue vertical bands with a coat of arms in the middle showing a quetzal bird.
gy: A green field with a yellow arrowhead and a red triangle at the hoist. The flag is nicknamed the Golden Arrowhead.
hn: Blue, white and blue bands, with five blue stars on the white — the five countries that once formed a single federation.
hr: Red, white and blue bands with a coat of arms in the middle showing a red and white chequerboard.
ht: Blue and red bands with a white square in the middle holding the arms: a palm tree, cannons and flags.
hu: Red, white and green bands: strength, faithfulness and hope.
id: A red band above a white one. Monaco's flag looks the same — only the proportions differ.
in: Saffron, white and green bands, with a blue 24-spoked wheel on the white — the Ashoka Chakra, a sign of motion and law.
ie: Green, white and orange vertical stripes. The white between them stands for peace between two communities.
ir: Green, white and red bands with a red emblem in the middle and an inscription repeated many times along the edges of the white band.
iq: Red, white and black bands with a green Arabic inscription on the white one.
is: A blue field with a red cross edged in white: blue for the sea, white for ice, red for volcanic fire.
il: A white field with two blue stripes and a blue six-pointed Star of David. The stripes recall the tallit prayer shawl.
it: Green, white and red vertical stripes, inspired by Napoleon's tricolour with the blue swapped for green.
jm: A gold diagonal cross splits the flag into green and black parts. It is the only national flag with no red, white or blue.
jo: Black, white and green bands with a red triangle at the hoist holding a white seven-pointed star.
jp: A white field with a red disc — the rising sun. The country's name means exactly that: origin of the sun.
kz: A sky-blue field with a golden sun and a steppe eagle beneath it, and a national ornament along the hoist.
ke: Black, red and green bands separated by white lines, with a Maasai shield and two spears in the middle.
kg: A red field with a yellow forty-rayed sun, and in its middle the tunduk, the wooden crown at the top of a yurt.
kh: Blue bands top and bottom, red in the middle, and on it the white temple of Angkor Wat — the only flag whose main image is a real building.
kr: A white field with the red and blue taegeuk circle in the middle and four black trigram symbols in the corners.
xk: A blue field with the gold outline of the territory and six white stars above it.
kw: Green, white and red bands with a black trapezoid at the hoist — the pan-Arab colours.
la: Red bands top and bottom, blue in the middle and a white disc — the moon over the Mekong.
lb: Red bands top and bottom, white in the middle, and on it a green Lebanon cedar.
lr: Eleven red and white stripes and a blue square with a single white star. It resembles the American flag because settlers from the USA founded the country.
ly: Red, black and green bands, with a white crescent and star on the black.
lk: A dark red field with a golden lion holding a sword, four bo leaves in the corners, and green and orange bands at the hoist.
ls: Blue, white and green bands with a black mokorotlo straw hat in the middle.
lt: Yellow, green and red bands: sun and fields, forests, blood and courage.
lu: Red, white and light blue bands. It differs from the Dutch flag by its lighter blue.
lv: A dark red field with a narrow white band across the middle. The shade is known as Latvian red.
ma: A red field with a green five-pointed star drawn as one interlaced line.
mc: A red band above a white one — almost the same as Indonesia's, only shorter.
md: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands with an eagle in the middle, a cross in its beak and an aurochs head on its shield.
mg: A white band at the hoist with red and green bands beside it.
mx: Green, white and red bands, with arms on the white: an eagle on a cactus holding a snake in its beak.
mk: A red field with a yellow sun whose eight broad rays reach the edges.
ml: Green, yellow and red vertical stripes.
mm: Yellow, green and red bands with a large white star across them.
me: A red field with a gold border and a crowned golden double-headed eagle in the middle.
mn: Red bands at the sides, blue in the middle, and the golden soyombo at the hoist — fire, sun, moon and other symbols.
mz: Green, black and yellow bands with a red triangle at the hoist holding a star, a book, a hoe and a rifle.
mr: A green field with a gold crescent and star, and red bands top and bottom.
mw: Black, red and green bands with a red rising sun on the black.
my: Fourteen red and white stripes and a blue canton with a yellow crescent and a fourteen-pointed star, one point per part of the country.
na: Blue and green parts split by a red diagonal band, with a golden rayed sun in the upper corner.
nc: Blue, red and green bands with a yellow disc holding the black roof-spear emblem of a traditional house. The French tricolour is flown alongside it here.
ne: Orange, white and green bands with an orange disc in the middle — the sun over the Sahara.
ng: Green, white and green vertical bands: green for fields and forests, white for peace.
ni: Blue, white and blue bands with arms in the middle: a triangle, volcanoes and a rainbow.
nl: Red, white and blue bands. The top stripe was once orange, but the dye faded quickly in the sun.
no: A blue cross edged in white on red: Swedish colours set inside the Danish flag.
np: The world's only national flag that is not a rectangle: two pennants stacked together, bearing a white moon and sun.
nz: A blue field with the British flag in the corner and four red stars edged in white — the Southern Cross.
om: White, red and green bands with a red band at the hoist and the national emblem in the corner: a khanjar dagger over two swords.
pk: A green field with a white crescent and star, and a white band at the hoist standing for the country's religious minorities.
pa: The flag is quartered: white squares with a blue and a red star, plus a blue and a red one.
pe: Red, white and red vertical bands. The coat of arms appears only on the state version of the flag.
ph: Blue and red bands with a white triangle at the hoist holding a sun and three stars. In wartime the flag is flown upside down, red on top.
pg: The flag is split diagonally: the Southern Cross on the black half, a golden bird-of-paradise on the red.
pl: A white band on top, red below. The colours come from the coat of arms: a white eagle on a red field.
pr: Red and white stripes with a blue triangle at the hoist holding a white star — like Cuba's, with the colours swapped.
kp: Blue bands top and bottom, a wide red band between them, and a red five-pointed star in a white disc.
pt: Green and red fields with an armillary sphere between them — an old navigator's instrument — and a shield with castles and smaller shields.
py: Red, white and blue bands with an emblem in the middle. This flag has a different emblem on the reverse — no other flag does.
ps: Black, white and green bands with a red triangle at the hoist — the pan-Arab colours.
qa: A maroon field with a white band at the hoist ending in nine saw-like points.
ro: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands. It differs from Chad's flag by a slightly lighter blue.
ru: White, blue and red bands. This tricolour was flown on the first Russian ships back in the 17th century.
rw: Blue, yellow and green bands with a golden rayed sun in the upper corner.
eh: Black, white and green bands with a red triangle at the hoist and a red crescent and star in the middle.
sa: A green field with a white Arabic inscription and a sword beneath it. This flag is never flown at half-mast, because the words are held sacred.
sd: Red, white and black bands with a green triangle at the hoist.
ss: Black, red and green bands separated by white lines, with a blue triangle at the hoist holding a gold star.
sn: Green, yellow and red vertical bands with a green star in the middle.
sb: Blue and green parts split by a yellow diagonal band, with five white stars in the upper corner.
sl: Green, white and blue bands: the land, peace and the sea.
sv: Blue, white and blue bands with arms in the middle: a triangle, volcanoes and a rainbow.
so: A light blue field with a white five-pointed star. The colour came from the UN flag, and the points stand for Somali lands.
rs: Red, blue and white bands with the coat of arms towards the hoist: a double-headed eagle and a shield with four firesteels.
sr: Green, white and red bands with a yellow star in the middle.
sk: White, blue and red bands with the arms towards the hoist: a double cross on three hills.
si: White, blue and red bands with arms towards the hoist showing the outline of Mount Triglav and waves.
se: A yellow cross on blue, shifted towards the hoist like every Nordic flag.
sz: Blue bands top and bottom, red in the middle, bearing an Nguni shield with spears and a staff.
sy: Green, white and black bands with three red stars in the middle. This flag became the national one only recently.
td: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands — almost identical to Romania's, but with a darker blue.
tg: Five green and yellow stripes with a red square and a white star in the corner.
th: Red and white bands with a wide blue one in the middle: the people, the faith and the king.
tj: Red, white and green bands, with a gold crown and seven stars on the white.
tm: A green field with a crescent and five stars, and a carpet band at the hoist showing the five main tribal patterns.
tl: A red field with a yellow triangle at the hoist, a black one over it, and a white star in the black.
tt: A red field with a black diagonal band edged in white: fire, earth and water.
tn: A red field with a white disc holding a red crescent and star.
tr: A red field with a white crescent and a five-pointed star.
tw: A red field with a blue canton holding a white sun of twelve rays — the twelve hours of the old way of counting time.
tz: Green and blue parts split by a black diagonal band edged in yellow.
ug: Six black, yellow and red bands with a grey crowned crane in a white disc.
ua: A blue band on top, yellow below: the sky above a wheat field.
uy: Nine white and blue stripes with the Sun of May in a white canton. The nine stripes are the regions the country began with.
us: Thirteen stripes for the first colonies and fifty stars for today's states, added one by one as the country grew.
uz: Blue, white and green bands with red lines, and a crescent with twelve stars in the corner.
ve: Yellow, blue and red bands, with eight white stars arcing across the blue.
vn: A red field with a large yellow five-pointed star.
vu: Red and green parts, a black triangle at the hoist and a yellow shape like a sideways Y, with a boar's tusk in the triangle.
ye: Red, white and black bands — the pan-Arab colours with no emblem at all.
za: A green sideways Y edged in white and gold, with red, blue and black parts around it. Six colours — more than any other national flag.
zm: A green field with red, black and orange stripes at the fly and an orange eagle above them.
zw: Seven stripes with a white triangle at the hoist holding a red star and the Zimbabwe Bird.
va: A square flag: yellow and white halves, with crossed keys and a tiara on the white.
sm: White and light blue bands with a coat of arms in the middle showing three towers on three peaks.
li: Blue and red bands with a gold crown in the upper corner, added after the 1936 Olympics revealed the flag matched Haiti's.
ad: Blue, yellow and red vertical bands with a coat of arms in the middle.
mt: White and red vertical halves with a grey George Cross edged in red in the upper corner.
nr: A blue field with a yellow stripe for the equator and a white twelve-pointed star below it: the island lies just south of the line.
tv: A light blue field with the British flag in the corner and nine yellow stars, one for each island.
pw: A light blue field with a yellow disc set towards the hoist — the moon over the ocean.
mh: A blue field with two widening diagonal bands, orange and white, and a white star of 24 points.
fm: A light blue field with four white stars, one for each part of the country.
ws: A red field with a blue canton holding the Southern Cross in five white stars.
to: A red field with a white canton bearing a red cross.
ki: A red upper half with a golden sun and a frigatebird above it, and blue and white waves below.
kn: Green and red parts split by a black diagonal band edged in yellow, with two white stars on the band.
gd: A red border with six stars, yellow and green triangles, a star in a disc at the centre and a nutmeg at the hoist.
vc: Blue, yellow and green vertical bands, with three green diamonds on the yellow arranged as a V.
bb: Blue, yellow and blue vertical bands with a broken black trident in the middle.
ag: A red field with a V shape in the middle made of black, blue and white bands, and a golden rising sun.
lc: A blue field with a black triangle edged in white and a yellow triangle in front of it — the Piton mountains above the sea.
mv: A red field with a green rectangle in the middle holding a white crescent.
sc: Five rays fan out from the lower hoist corner: blue, yellow, red, white and green.
sg: Red and white bands with a white crescent and five stars in a circle in the corner.
bh: A white band at the hoist and a red field, with a five-pointed zigzag between them for the five pillars of Islam.
